info.name: Conversation Assignment API
info.description:
Postman collection for the Conversation Assignment API (NestJS and MongoDB).

**Before you run it**
1. Start MongoDB and the API (see the README): `docker compose up -d --wait`, then `npx nx serve api`.
2. Import this file into Postman.
3. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, in order. Later folders use the ids that earlier requests save as collection variables.

**Authentication.** There is no login. Each request sends three headers: `x-user-id`, `x-workspace-id` and `x-role`, taken from the variables below. Requests that need another role or workspace override them.

**Variables.** The defaults below are collection variables. For a different host, user or workspace, import `postman/local.postman_environment.json`, edit its values and select it: an environment value overrides the collection default, so nothing in the collection needs changing.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:3000` | Where the API runs |
| `userId` | `user_123` | The acting user, recorded as `assignedBy` |
| `workspaceId` | `workspace_1` | The caller's workspace |
| `role` | `manager` | `admin`, `manager` or `agent` |
| `adminUserId` | `user_admin` | A second user, used for the admin requests |
| `otherWorkspaceId` | `workspace_2` | A different workspace, for isolation checks |
| `unknownId` | `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` | A well-formed id that does not exist |

The remaining variables (`agentId`, `agent2Id`, `foreignAgentId`, `conversationId`, `closedConversationId`, `nextToken` and the others) are filled in by test scripts while the collection runs. Agent emails are generated per run, so the collection can be run repeatedly against the same database.

**Ids.** Ids are 24-character hex strings. The specification's examples such as `conv_123` are rejected with 400, and some requests send them on purpose.

**Command line.** `npx newman run postman/assignment-api.postman_collection.json` runs every request and its tests.

item.name: Authentication

request.description: No `x-user-id`, `x-workspace-id` or `x-role` header.
`x-role` must be `admin`, `manager` or `agent`.

item.description: The mock guard reads three headers. A missing header or an unknown role is rejected with 401 before anything else runs.

request.description: The email is trimmed and lower-cased, and must be unique within the workspace. The pre-request script makes it unique per run, in mixed case so the lower-casing is visible.
The same email in the same workspace, enforced by a unique index.

exec: pm.test("error body is 409 Conflict", () => { pm.expect(body.statusCode).to.eql(409); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Conflict"); pm.expect(body).to.have.property("message"); });
pm.test("error body is 400 Bad Request", () => { pm.expect(body.statusCode).to.eql(400); pm.expect(body.error).to.eql("Bad Request"); pm.expect(body).to.have.property("message"); });

request.description: Used later to reassign the conversation.
An agent in a different workspace, used to prove cross-workspace assignment is rejected.
Newest first. `next` is an opaque token for the following page.

exec: pm.test("one item and a next token", () => { pm.expect(body.items).to.have.length(1); pm.expect(body.hasNext).to.be.true; pm.expect(body.hasPrevious).to.be.false; });

pm.test("a different agent, with a way back", () => { pm.expect(body.items).to.have.length(1); pm.expect(body.items[0].id).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("pageOneAgentId")); pm.expect(body.hasPrevious).to.be.true; });

request.description: `assignedBy` and the workspace come from the auth headers, never from the body.

item.name: Assign the same agent again (no change)

request.description: Even when an admin repeats the assignment, `assignedAt`, `assignedBy` and `updatedAt` do not change.

exec: pm.test("only conversations of that agent", () => { pm.expect(body.items.map(c => c.id)).to.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("conversationId")); body.items.forEach(c => pm.expect(c.assignedAgentId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("agentId"))); });

request.description: Admins and managers may assign. The new agent, time and user replace the previous ones.
